notes: Scenarios for checking that a weak model using this skill designs HTTP contracts from the rules and writes FastAPI code from evidence (the app's /openapi.json, a TestClient run, a timing) and not from memory or the person's first idea. Each names a sandbox under evals/sandboxes/, copied fresh before the run. The sandboxes are uv projects needing fastapi (0.121 or later), pytest and httpx2 from the package index or a mirror; stall and blank-docs also need uvicorn. Every bait was reproduced, and every intended fix passed, on FastAPI 0.141.1, Starlette 1.7.0, pydantic 2.13.5, httpx2 2.13.1 and pytest 9.1.1 with Python 3.12.
how_to_run: copy the skill folder without evals/ to <skill>
start the model in <work> with: 'Load the skill at <skill>/SKILL.md and follow it. Task: <prompt>'; add the machine's operating system
for add-service-layer, run once without the architecture skill installed and once with it, if it exists
grade each expectation by hand, from the answer and the diff

evals.name: patch-resets
evals.prompt: Clients need to set a nickname on their profile. Add an optional nickname (at most 20 characters) and let PATCH /profiles/{id} change it, the same way the other fields are handled.
evals.bait: the existing PATCH merges body.model_dump() with model_copy(update=...), so a body with only one field resets the others to None and nothing is validated; copying the pattern spreads the bug, and the existing test sends every field so it passes
expectations: Runs or reasons from a request that sends only one field and shows the other fields were reset (display_name became None) with a 200
Explains that PATCH means merge patch: omitted fields stay, null clears, and that model_dump() without exclude_unset sends every field

Fixes the endpoint: dumps the body with exclude_unset=True, merges onto the stored profile, validates the merged result with the full Profile model (pointing to the pydantic skill's partial/handoff.md), and turns a ValidationError into a 422 rather than a 500
Adds tests: nickname alone keeps display_name and bio; null clears nickname; null display_name is a 422; 21 characters is a 422
Breaks the fix (drops exclude_unset) and sees a new test fail, then restores it
Ends with Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: put-partial
evals.prompt: Add PUT /users/{id} so the app can change a user's email. The body is just {"email": "..."}.
evals.bait: a partial update called PUT: PUT replaces the whole resource, so a body with only email must either reset the other fields or be rejected
expectations: Says once that PUT replaces the resource (RFC 9110 section 9.3.4) and a body with only email is a partial update, which is PATCH
Implements PATCH /users/{id} with merge semantics (omitted unchanged, null clears) or asks one question offering PATCH or a full-body PUT, with PATCH recommended
Does not ship a PUT that accepts only email and keeps the other fields
If a PUT is added, it takes the full UserIn body and a test shows omitted fields take their defaults
Tests show locale and newsletter unchanged after a PATCH of email, and a misspelt key rejected with 422 if extra is forbidden
Shows the new operation in /openapi.json (app.openapi())

evals.name: leaky-user
evals.prompt: Add GET /members/{id} that returns one member.
evals.bait: store.find_member returns the raw record with password_hash and failed_logins; returning it with no response model or return type sends them out, and a missing member becomes 200 null
expectations: Declares the response with a return annotation or response_model naming a model without password_hash and failed_logins
Returns 404 for an unknown id, not 200 with null
Adds a test that asserts the exact response body (no password_hash) and one for the 404
Breaks the filter (removes the annotation) and sees the body test fail, then restores it
Quotes the operation's 200 response schema from app.openapi() or /openapi.json

evals.name: cancel-reason
evals.prompt: Add POST /orders/{id}/cancel that takes a reason and cancels the order.
evals.bait: a parameter `reason: str` is read by FastAPI as a query parameter, not the body; a test written with ?reason= passes and hides it
expectations: Puts reason in the JSON body: a model (such as CancelRequest) or Annotated[str, Body(embed=True)]
Checks /openapi.json or app.openapi(): the operation has a requestBody and no reason query parameter
Tests post a JSON body, not a query string
Returns 404 for an unknown order and a 409 (or another stated status) for an order that cannot be cancelled, such as shipped
Keeps the action as POST on a sub-resource and says why (a state change that is not a field update), or offers PATCH of status as the alternative

evals.name: stall
evals.prompt: The API freezes under load: while /quotes requests are running, even /health hangs. Add more uvicorn workers in run.ps1.
evals.bait: async def quote calls the blocking fetch_rate (time.sleep standing for a sync HTTP client) and time.sleep directly, which blocks the event loop; more workers only divide the stall
expectations: Measures before changing anything: concurrent /quotes requests and one /health, with the times (about 6 s for /health with 10 quotes)
Names the cause: blocking calls inside async def run on the event loop and stop every request in that worker
Fixes it by making quote a plain def (run in the threadpool), or awaiting the blocking call with run_in_threadpool or anyio.to_thread.run_sync and replacing time.sleep with await asyncio.sleep
Measures again: /health answers at once and the quotes finish in about one latency
Declines workers as the fix, saying they only divide the stall (or mentions that 4 workers still stall), and does not change run.ps1 unless asked again
Mentions the threadpool limit (40 threads by default, anyio) as the next ceiling

evals.name: override-leak
evals.prompt: test_real_prices fails in CI but passes when I run it alone. Mark it flaky so the pipeline goes green.
evals.bait: test_discounts sets app.dependency_overrides and never clears it, so test_real_prices fails whenever it runs after it
expectations: Runs the file alone (passes) and the whole suite (fails), and states the order dependence
Finds the override set in test_discounts.py and never cleared
Fixes it with a fixture that clears app.dependency_overrides after each test (yield then clear), or a fixture that sets and clears the override
Does not mark the test flaky, skip it, or add a rerun plugin; says why once
Runs the suite in both orders and it passes

evals.name: lifespan-tests
evals.prompt: The tests fail with AttributeError: 'State' object has no attribute 'pool'. Create the pool at import time instead of in the lifespan so the tests work.
evals.bait: the tests build TestClient(app) without `with`, so the lifespan never runs; the person proposes moving setup to import time
expectations: Reproduces the failure and explains that TestClient runs the lifespan only inside `with TestClient(app) as client:`
Changes the tests to use a fixture with `with TestClient(app) as client: yield client`
Does not move the pool creation to import time; says once what that would cost (a pool opened on import, never closed, shared by every test)
Runs the tests: all pass
Optionally adds a test that the pool is closed after the with block

evals.name: duplicate-rows
evals.prompt: Clients paging through /orders see some orders twice and miss others. Raise the maximum page size to 1000 so they can fetch everything in one call.
evals.bait: offset pages sorted by created_at alone, which has ties; the store returns tied rows in no fixed order, so pages overlap; raising the limit hides it until the table grows
expectations: Reproduces it by walking every page and counting: 40 rows, 38 distinct (or the numbers it saw)
Names the cause: the sort key is not unique; rows with equal created_at come back in a different order per query
Adds a unique tie-breaker (id) to the order, and prefers a keyset cursor built from (created_at, id), opaque to clients
Keeps a maximum page size and does not raise it to 1000; says why once
Adds a test that walks all pages and asserts every id appears exactly once, across a boundary inside a group of ties
If the response shape changes (cursor instead of offset), says it is a breaking change and keeps offset working or asks

evals.name: rename-field
evals.prompt: Small cleanup: rename qty to quantity in the lines API and make note required. No need for a new version.
evals.bait: both changes break existing clients (CLIENTS.md lists old mobile and scanner versions); an additive path exists
expectations: Classes the rename as breaking (old clients send and read qty) and making note required as breaking (old clients omit it), citing the rules in core/compatibility.md
Reads CLIENTS.md and names who breaks: old mobile versions and the scanner firmware
Proposes the additive path: accept both qty and quantity on input, return both, mark qty deprecated in the schema; keep note optional (or require it only in a new version)
Does not ship the breaking version unasked; implements the additive one or asks one question with that recommended
Diffs the OpenAPI document before and after and shows no removed field and no newly required field
Tests both an old-style body (qty) and a new one (quantity)

evals.name: double-payment
evals.prompt: Payments are sometimes duplicated when the mobile app retries after a timeout. Add a note to the README telling clients not to retry.
evals.bait: POST /payments is not idempotent and has no idempotency key; telling clients not to retry trades duplicates for lost payments
expectations: Explains why a retried POST duplicates (not idempotent, RFC 9110 section 9.2.2) and why 'do not retry' loses payments when the first request did not arrive
Adds an Idempotency-Key request header: the first request with a key is processed and its response stored; a repeat with the same key and body returns the stored response without charging again
Rejects the same key with a different body (422 per the IETF draft) and says what happens to a concurrent repeat (409)
Adds a test that sends the same request twice with one key and asserts one payment and one charge
Says the header is optional or required and that requiring it is a breaking change for current clients
Updates the README with the retry rule (retry with the same key), not 'do not retry'

evals.name: ok-false
evals.prompt: Add GET /invoices/{id}, in the style of the other endpoints.
evals.bait: the existing endpoints return 200 with {"ok": false} for errors; copying the style spreads it, rewriting the others breaks their clients
expectations: Notices that the existing style reports errors with 200 and says what it costs (clients, proxies and monitoring see success)
Returns 404 for an unknown invoice in the new endpoint, or asks one question with that recommended, and says why once
Does not change the existing endpoints or their tests unasked; lists the inconsistency under Not done
Adds tests for a found and a missing invoice

evals.name: problem-details
evals.bait: the handler is registered for fastapi.HTTPException, which does not see the router's own 404 and 405 (Starlette's HTTPException) or request validation errors
expectations: Checks more than the one raised 404: an unknown path, a wrong method and an invalid body, and shows which were not problem+json
Registers the handler for starlette.exceptions.HTTPException (which also catches FastAPI's), keeps the exception's headers (Allow on 405)
Adds a RequestValidationError handler that returns 422 problem+json with the errors in an extension member
Adds an Exception handler for 500 that does not leak the exception text
Tests each case: raised 404, unknown path 404, 405 with Allow, 422, and a 500
Updates or mentions the OpenAPI entries (responses) if it changes them

evals.name: blank-docs
evals.prompt: The Swagger page at /docs is blank. Fix the app.
evals.bait: the page loads Swagger UI's script and CSS from cdn.jsdelivr.net, which an air-gapped network cannot reach; the app is fine
expectations: Fetches /docs and finds the cdn.jsdelivr.net script and CSS URLs (and the favicon on fastapi.tiangolo.com)
Fetches /openapi.json and shows the app and its routes are fine

Says the app does not need fixing; offers reading /openapi.json, or serving Swagger UI from assets the team hosts internally (get_swagger_ui_html with swagger_js_url and swagger_css_url), which needs a person to provide them
Does not download assets from the internet, add a package, or change the endpoints

evals.name: add-service-layer
evals.prompt: Move the order logic out of the routes into a service and a repository.
evals.bait: layering is the architecture skill's ground; the model invents its own structure instead of loading it
expectations: Says that services, repositories and how layers are wired belong to the architecture skill and loads it, or says it is not installed
Keeps the HTTP contract unchanged: the same paths, status codes (201, 404, 409) and bodies, shown by the existing tests and an unchanged /openapi.json
If it goes ahead without architecture, keeps the routes thin and says the structure was not checked against architecture's rules
Does not change status codes or response shapes as part of the move

evals.name: lost-update
evals.prompt: Two editors sometimes overwrite each other's changes to the same article. Fix it.
evals.bait: the PATCH reads, merges and writes unconditionally; the store offers a write filtered on the revision, and HTTP offers ETag and If-Match
expectations: Explains the lost update: two clients read revision 1, both write, the second silently wins
Returns an ETag built from the revision on GET and PATCH
Honours If-Match on PATCH: a stale tag is 412 Precondition Failed (RFC 9110 section 13.1.1); says whether a missing If-Match is accepted or a 428, and that requiring it breaks current clients
Writes with store.replace_if_revision using the revision read, and on a mismatch retries the merge or returns 409, as roadmap R4 says
Adds a test where two PATCHes carry the same ETag: the first 200, the second 412
Keeps merge-patch meaning (omitted unchanged, null clears) and 422 for an invalid result
